title: Rav Huna son of Rav Hoshaya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Horayot 3b](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.3b.2); Hyman suggests that perhaps the reading should be “son of Rav Yehoshua.” In [Yalkut, Mishlei, remez 954](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.954.1): “Rav Huna bar Hoshaya said: and it crowns him like the awn on an ear of grain.” But the statement is in [Sotah 5a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.5a.16), and there it is Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua.[^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson digital Sotah 5a compares a small amount of pride adorning a scholar to the awn adorning an ear of grain: ליה refers to the scholar. It explicitly has Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua; Horayot 3b has Hoshaya. Hyman’s suggested emendation remains tentative.

Horayot names Hoshaya in a discussion of unanimous rulings. The Yalkut and Sotah both give the comparison to an awn on an ear of grain, but the Yalkut names Hoshaya and Sotah names Yehoshua. Hyman proposes the name Yehoshua tentatively.
